comments.author: macuseri686
comments.body:
Using a normal AI model like Nano Banana or GPT image 2 wont work for assets such as spritesheets, because AI models cant output transparency, and image models alone have no understanding of animation.

That is actually why I built GameLab Studio ([https://gamelabstudio.co](https://gamelabstudio.co)). It’s designed for game assets and it’ll generate consistent pixel-art sprites, animations and full transparent bg spritesheets for anything.

https://i.redd.it/co8xs01ee7zg1.gif

Gamelabs Studio MCP plugs right into your agent like Cursor, to enable rapid iteration right in your code editor

[https://gamelabstudio.co/blog/mcp-setup-guide](https://gamelabstudio.co/blog/mcp-setup-guide)

It also enforces consistency across scale, palette, and angles, by using already generated angles of the same asset for reference, so you don’t end up with “AI asset soup” during prototyping.

We also have a seamless tileable edge-aware texture generation model

**Gamelabs Studio has been used in real production game releases, like** [https://www.crazygames.com/game/age-of-steam-tower-defence?bypassCache=hgp3p](https://www.crazygames.com/game/age-of-steam-tower-defence?bypassCache=hgp3p)

replies.author: macuseri686
replies.body:
Thanks for the feedback.

when you say "color shift" are you talking about the whole animation output having its entire color everywhere shifted?

or are you referring to small areas of color fringing around the edges, leftover from the chroma key process?

if its the latter, 2 things you can do to reduce this:

1. use the high quality animation option in the generate animation dialog.  
2. in the spritesheet generation dialog, under the manual tab, turn off auto chroma key threshold, and set it a bit higher to something like 80

replies.author: macuseri686
replies.body: Ah, that’s because it’s exported as a GIF for Reddit. The GIF format limits colors to 256 colors, as opposed to PNG that supports full 32bit color. When you export as a sprite sheet on the platform it uses png.

Is there some way for this?

replies.author: macuseri686
replies.body:
Hi designer drummer,

Thank you for the compliment. Much appreciated 

Yes, it’s definitely frustrating when AI sometimes gets just one thing wrong, or hallucinates.

We do actually have a built in editor right in Gamelabs Studio for both images and animations.  
You can easily just click the edit button underneath the generated image or animation. There you can touch up and erase a small mistake the ai made, or even trim, cut and splice the animation sequence.

comments.author: Terrible-Bag9495
comments.body:
Sprite sheets are a different beast than single image gen tbh. the consistency problem is less about prompts and more about workflow. if you're doing pixel art sprites, Aseprite with manual cleanup after AI generation is probaly the most reliable pipeline.

for pose control specifically, ControlNet can lock down limb positions frame to frame which helps a lot. Mage Space handles character consistency across outputs too if you want a browser option.

comments.author: Far-Travel-5206
comments.body: common wall - AI sprites tend to drift a lot so your character never quite matches frame to frame. one workaround is to stop relying on prompts and lock in a single source model first, then generate all your animations from that. you can try smth like Reallusion, it can help with that since you keep one rigged character and just export different animations/angles, then convert to sprites if needed. bit more setup upfront, but way more consistent long-term.
